mapQuery: Trabocco Sasso della Cajana, Contrada Vallevo 64, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

address: Contrada Vallevo, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Isolata, Contrada Vallevo, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

name: Trabocco Punta Tufano
desc: April–October, famous brodetto — but its own site says dining is exclusively for organised groups and agencies. A couple must phone Rinaldo (333 4436831) and hope.
address: Contrada Vallevo 78, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Tufano, Contrada Vallevo 78, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Torre, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Cavalluccio, Contrada Piane Favaro 267, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Punciosa, Contrada Cavalluccio, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Rocciosa, Via Finocchieto 1, Fossacesia CH, Italy

mapQuery: Trabocco Pesce Palombo, SS16, Fossacesia Marina, Fossacesia CH, Italy

mapQuery: Trabocco Valle Grotte, SS16 km 482, San Vito Chietino CH, Italy

name: Trabocco Turchino
desc: D'Annunzio's one, from Il trionfo della morte. Council-owned since 1981. Free to see from the path; walking onto it needs a guided visit with Il Bosso, about €10.
address: Trabocco Turchino, San Vito Chietino CH, Italy
mapQuery: Trabocco Turchino, San Vito Chietino CH, Italy

name: Trabocco Punta Le Morge

mapQuery: Trabocco Punta Le Morge, Torino di Sangro CH, Italy

name: Trabocco Cungarelle

mapQuery: Trabocco Cungarelle, SS16 km 516, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria il Coccodrillo / Forno Zulli

The “Coccodrillo” itself is a metre-long filled pizza-bread with mortadella, invented here. Gluten-free dough too. Tue–Sun 19:00–23:00, closed Monday.
address: Via Mazzini 12, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Pizzeria il Coccodrillo / Forno Zulli, Via Mazzini 12, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria Piana del Sole
desc: Unpretentious contrada pizzeria going since 2005 with a big local following. Own list of originali plus classics and focacce. 19:30–24:00, closed Tuesday.
address: Contrada Villa Stanazzo 217, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Pizzeria Piana del Sole, Contrada Villa Stanazzo 217, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria Il Caminetto
desc: Family-run, genuine wood oven, cheap and well topped. Reviewers single out the crisp base and the house coppo — pasta and shellfish baked under a pizza-dough lid. 19:00–24:00, closed Tuesday.
address: Via della Marina 75, Fossacesia CH, Italy
mapQuery: Pizzeria Il Caminetto, Via della Marina 75, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: COCÒ Pizzeria
desc: Thin crisp base plus arrosticini, about €20 a head, on the lungomare. Out-of-season listings show only Thu–Sat 19:00–22:45, so call — and it may fold with the beach season mid-month.
mapQuery: COCÒ Pizzeria, Via Lungomare 145, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria Napule è
desc: The serious one nearby. Proper Verace Neapolitan — the pizzaiolo trained and now teaches at Verace Matura in Naples. In 50 Top Pizza Italia 2026 (Pizzerie Eccellenti). Dinner Tue–Sun, closed Monday. Book Fri/Sat.
address: Contrada Villa Andreoli 341, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Pizzeria Napule è, Contrada Villa Andreoli 341, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria Trattoria Ruhental
desc: Small contrada trattoria-pizzeria, the highest-rated pizza in Lanciano though on a thin review base. Two closing days, so plan it: Wed–Sat 19:15–23:00, Sun lunch and dinner, closed Monday and Tuesday.
mapQuery: Pizzeria Trattoria Ruhental, Via Follani 138, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Forno Susi
desc: Pizza al taglio, and the reference point for pizza lancianese — fourth-generation bakery praised for the lightness of the dough. The lunch answer rather than a dinner one. Mon–Sat 06:00–21:00, closed Sunday.
address: Via Luigi de Crecchio 82, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Forno Susi, Via Luigi de Crecchio 82, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria Il Sogno
desc: Artisan seasonal pizzas in mini and maxi format, five-grain wholemeal dough, arancini. Solid mid-range town option; hours aren’t published, so ring ahead.
address: Via F. Masciangelo 26, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Pizzeria Il Sogno, Via F. Masciangelo 26, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Kitchenetta
desc: Genuine wood oven, gluten-free options, and the best of a fairly ordinary Ortona field — nothing in Ortona, San Vito or Vasto makes any of the national guides.
mapQuery: Kitchenetta, Ortona CH, Italy

name: Osteria La Frasca
desc: 50 Top Pizza Italia 2026 (Pizzerie Eccellenti). Neapolitan-derived at 75% hydration, organic flours only, baked around 380 °C, with home-cured salumi — a guide-listed place that still feels like a country osteria. Closing day unpublished; phone.
address: Contrada San Giacomo 165, Scerni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Osteria La Frasca, Contrada San Giacomo 165, Scerni CH, Italy

name: Giangi Pizza e Ricerca
desc: The best pizza within easy reach: 30th in Italy in 50 Top Pizza 2026, Tre Spicchi and 92/100 from Gambero Rosso, plus their sustainability award. Gourmet but not stuffy, €7–25 a pizza. Tue–Sun 17:30–23:00, closed Monday. Books online, and you should.
address: Via Valle Arielli 27, Arielli CH, Italy
mapQuery: Giangi Pizza e Ricerca, Via Valle Arielli 27, Arielli CH, Italy

name: Black Wood Pub & Pizzeria
desc: 50 Top Pizza Italia 2026 (Pizzerie Eccellenti). Relaxed pub-pizzeria — good if you’re combining it with a Vasto day. Listings show open daily 19:30–24:00.
address: Via San Rocco 30, San Salvo CH, Italy
mapQuery: Black Wood Pub & Pizzeria, Via San Rocco 30, San Salvo CH, Italy

name: Pizzeria La Sorgente
desc: Tre Spicchi from Gambero Rosso for the twelfth year running, plus their 2026 national award for best drinks list. Gourmet, metre-long Roman style, huge beer and wine list — though recent reviews grumble at €18–20 pizzas. Mon–Fri lunch and dinner, Sat–Sun dinner only.
address: Via Antonio Gramsci 9, Guardiagrele CH, Italy
mapQuery: Pizzeria La Sorgente, Via Antonio Gramsci 9, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: Fermenta Pizzeria Gourmet
desc: 60th in Italy in 50 Top Pizza 2026 and Due Spicchi from Gambero Rosso. Padellino, contemporary and crisp styles, heavily Abruzzese sourcing — Pera d’Abruzzo tomato, pecorino di Farindola, heritage grains.
address: Viale Unita d'Italia 3, Chieti CH, Italy
mapQuery: Fermenta Pizzeria Gourmet, Viale Unita d'Italia 3, Chieti CH, Italy

name: Rabottini Pizza
desc: 50 Top Pizza Italia 2026 (Pizzerie Eccellenti). Only worth it if you’re already in Pescara for the evening — pair it with Scumm or Radicale.
address: Via Raffaello Sanzio 66, Pescara PE, Italy
mapQuery: Rabottini Pizza, Via Raffaello Sanzio 66, Pescara PE, Italy

name: Trattoria delle Frapa
desc: The nearest thing to a second Amici della Forchetta. Family-run, big antipasti, chitarra, arrosticini, garden seating. Closed Mondays.
address: Contrada Torre Sansone 120, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Trattoria delle Frapa, Contrada Torre Sansone 120, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Caniloro
desc: Working farm in olive groves. Own wine, cheese and flour; handmade pasta, rabbit over the fire, grilled lamb. Book ahead — hours aren't published.
mapQuery: Agriturismo Caniloro, Contrada Sant'Onofrio, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Il Grappolo
desc: Small family place 5 km from Lanciano, everything from their own produce. Low online profile — ring first. Same lane as Frapa if one's full.
address: Contrada Torre Sansone 141, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Agriturismo Il Grappolo, Contrada Torre Sansone 141, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Trattoria San Domenico
desc: Twenty seats on a terrace under the Aragonese castle. The brodetto all'ortonese is the dish. Set menus €25 to €48. Tiny, so book.
address: Vicolo San Domenico 1, Ortona CH, Italy
mapQuery: Trattoria San Domenico, Vicolo San Domenico 1, Ortona CH, Italy

name: Bio Agriturismo Le Mignole
desc: Certified organic farm restaurant, one of the best-rated places in the village. Mixed antipasti, homemade pasta, roast lamb. The Wednesday closure couldn't be verified — ring first.
mapQuery: Bio Agriturismo Le Mignole, Orsogna CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Le Magnolie
desc: Seven hectares, everything from their own land. This is the ventricina stop — cavatelli with ventricina sugo, sagne with duck, grilled lamb.
address: Via dei Palombari 54, Vasto CH, Italy
mapQuery: Agriturismo Le Magnolie, Via dei Palombari 54, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Il Podere del Carlone
desc: Rustic country restaurant among olives and vines with sea views. Grilled meats, ventricina, chitarra — and a €15 lunch menu.
address: Via San Lorenzo 340, Vasto CH, Italy
mapQuery: Il Podere del Carlone, Via San Lorenzo 340, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Trattoria da Ferri
desc: Old-school seafood trattoria in the historic centre, listed by the Accademia Italiana della Cucina, famous locally for its brodetto. Honest prices, no ceremony.
mapQuery: Trattoria da Ferri, Via Osca 58, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Travaglini
desc: Pallotte cacio e ova, chitarra with duck ragù, rabbit with potatoes, own Montepulciano fermented in open vats. Reservation-only — not a walk-in.
address: Contrada Piano delle Vigne, Casoli CH, Italy
mapQuery: Agriturismo Travaglini, Contrada Piano delle Vigne, Casoli CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Colle Tripio
desc: Hillside farm with sea views. Arrosticini, grilled lamb, homemade ricotta, off-menu daily specials, and cheap. Closed Mondays; listings show Sunday lunch and dinner both served.
address: Villa San Vincenzo, Guardiagrele CH, Italy
mapQuery: Agriturismo Colle Tripio, Villa San Vincenzo, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: La Macelleria di Romantino
desc: Third-generation butcher with a dining room attached. Grilled meats, pasta with lamb meatballs, house salumi. Small — book. Closed Mondays.
address: Via Modesto della Porta 35, Guardiagrele CH, Italy
mapQuery: La Macelleria di Romantino, Via Modesto della Porta 35, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Pesolillo
desc: Vineyard estate with a restaurant open to all. Hand-cut arrosticini from selected sheep meat are the reason to go. Also does big events, so check they're not booked out.
address: Strada Colle Rotondo 45, Chieti CH, Italy
mapQuery: Agriturismo Pesolillo, Strada Colle Rotondo 45, Chieti CH, Italy

name: Villa Maiella
desc: The splurge. One Michelin star, family-run since 1968, rooted in Abruzzese peasant cooking — their own charcuterie, Majella herbs, lamb. Book weeks ahead.
address: Via Sette Dolori 30, Guardiagrele CH, Italy
mapQuery: Villa Maiella, Via Sette Dolori 30, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Il Feudo
desc: Majella foothills, right under the Valle dell'Avello cliffs. Antipasto spreads, pappardelle, roast meats, homemade dolci. Closed Wednesdays.
mapQuery: Agriturismo Il Feudo, Via Raiese 36, Pennapiedimonte CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Tholos
desc: Up in the Majella above the Santo Spirito hermitage. Black piglet braised in Montepulciano, spelt polenta, homemade tarts. Around €40pp, booking essential. Pair with the eremi.
mapQuery: Agriturismo Tholos, Roccamorice PE, Italy

name: Cantina Frentana
desc: Your local co-op — 400 growers, and a mad 1960s concrete wine tower with a tasting room and balcony at the top, best at sunset. Shop sells bottles walk-in; the tower is reservation only. Hours conflict across sources, so phone: 0872 60152.
address: Contrada Perazza 32, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Cantina Frentana, Contrada Perazza 32, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

name: La Vinarte
desc: The nearest winery of any. Guided cellar and vineyard tour plus five wines with bread, oil, salumi and cheese, from €25.
mapQuery: La Vinarte, Santa Maria Imbaro CH, Italy

name: BP Service
desc: Closest real minivan-and-driver operator. Mercedes V-Class, Sprinters, 9-seat vans, and they list private tours and hourly hire. Ask for a full-day servizio a disposizione, priced per vehicle not per head.
mapQuery: BP Service, Contrada Severini 5, Treglio CH, Italy

name: Green Road Bike
desc: E-bike tasting ride on the Via Verde — 42 km, flat, with a winery stop plus cheese, salumi and honey. They collect and drop the bikes. Solves the who-drives problem entirely.
mapQuery: Green Road Bike, Lido Saraceni, Ortona CH, Italy

name: Agriverde
desc: Certified organic since 1988, well ahead of EU rules. Restaurant and wellness centre attached, so it doubles as lunch.
address: Caldari di Ortona, Ortona CH, Italy
mapQuery: Agriverde, Caldari di Ortona, Ortona CH, Italy

name: Feudo Antico
desc: The reference producer for the tiny Tullum DOCG. Organic, spontaneous-ferment lines, strong Pecorino, and a Roman villa with a museum on site.
mapQuery: Feudo Antico, Tollo CH, Italy

name: Fontefico
desc: Small organic family estate, and the one that actually runs a harvest experience in September — six hours, €110pp. Book at least three days ahead.
mapQuery: Fontefico, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Tenuta Ulisse
desc: The slick modern one — best-appointed tasting space nearby, polished Montepulciano, Cerasuolo and Pecorino.
mapQuery: Tenuta Ulisse, Crecchio CH, Italy

name: Cantina Orsogna 1964
desc: Italy's largest biodynamic co-op. Worth an enquiry if the biodynamic thing appeals.
mapQuery: Cantina Orsogna 1964, Orsogna CH, Italy

name: Italia Sweet Italia — Fabrizio Lucci
desc: The strongest wine-tour lead by a distance: driver, transport and lunch included, small groups up to 12. Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice 2026 with a 5.0 rating. Email him directly rather than booking through a marketplace — you'll get a custom Trabocchi-coast day.
mapQuery: Italia Sweet Italia — Fabrizio Lucci, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Cascina del Colle
desc: The clearest offer of the lot: cellar tour plus three wines plus a board of their own produce and oil, €35pp, 90 minutes, online calendar booking, English available.
mapQuery: Cascina del Colle, Villamagna CH, Italy

name: Masciarelli
desc: The big Abruzzo name that's still close. Three barrel cellars, then tasting with local produce at the beautiful Castello di Semivicoli.
address: San Martino sulla Marrucina CH, Italy
mapQuery: Masciarelli, San Martino sulla Marrucina CH, Italy

name: Agricola Tiberio
desc: Cristiana Tiberio's old-vine Trebbiano Abruzzese at 350 m is among the most talked-about whites in Italy. Small and serious — request, don't turn up.
mapQuery: Agricola Tiberio, Cugnoli PE, Italy

name: Torre dei Beati
desc: Certified organic and slightly cult — Cocciapazza, Rosa-ae. Loreto Aprutino is the classic Abruzzo pilgrimage hilltown. Email well in advance.
mapQuery: Torre dei Beati, Loreto Aprutino PE, Italy

name: De Fermo
desc: Fully biodynamic, one of the region's serious natural-leaning producers, in a lovely old estate. Pair it with Torre dei Beati in one day.
mapQuery: De Fermo, Loreto Aprutino PE, Italy

name: Emidio Pepe
desc: The legend. Hand-destemmed, glass-lined concrete, a library of Trebbiano and Montepulciano going back decades. Worth the drive if you want one pilgrimage.
mapQuery: Emidio Pepe, Torano Nuovo TE, Italy

name: Corso di cucina — nonna Filomena
desc: Your nearest class, at a small winery. An hour making pasta alla chitarra or bocconotti or pizza scima, then a picnic in the vines with antipasto contadino and wine. From €45pp, about three hours, minimum four. Books online with the date confirmed within 48 hours.
mapQuery: Corso di cucina — nonna Filomena, Santa Maria Imbaro CH, Italy

name: Frantoio Giocondo
desc: Family olive mill above the coast — Tour of the plant plus a guided sensory oil tasting, and it works outside the pressing season, so September is fine. Reported at ~€7pp — not published, so confirm when you call +39 347 1656911.
mapQuery: Frantoio Giocondo, San Vito Chietino CH, Italy

name: Agriturismo Caniloro — cooking
desc: The closest thing to your Amici della Forchetta instinct: pick vegetables in their kitchen garden, take them to the lab and cook Frentano peasant dishes, including cooking over open fire and sotto il coppo. From €45pp, three hours. Minimum ten, but offer to pay for six or eight and it’s usually negotiable.
mapQuery: Agriturismo Caniloro — cooking, Contrada Sant'Onofrio, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Feudo Antico — Cantine Aperte in Vendemmia
desc: Properly hands-on: 10:00 cellar tour, then picking and pressing Montepulciano, then a 13:00 picnic with pallotte cacio e ova and gnocchetti. Around €35 adult and €15 child at the 2024 edition — which fell on the fourth Sunday of September, after your window. No 2026 date is published; ring 340 8469682, and if it lands on the 20th it decides your last Sunday.
mapQuery: Feudo Antico — Cantine Aperte in Vendemmia, Tollo CH, Italy

name: Fontefico — cooking class
desc: Two recipes cooked with the family, then a four-course wine-paired lunch on the estate. €95pp, four hours, and it runs Friday to Sunday — which covers the 11th, 12th, 13th, 18th, 19th and 20th. WhatsApp +39 335 7124154.
mapQuery: Fontefico — cooking class, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Accademia della Ventricina
desc: Slow Food Presidium producer of ventricina del Vastese, and the site says plainly that anyone who asks can visit the premises. No packaged tour — it’s a phone call to 339 3086378. There’s also a bookable one-hour guided ventricina tasting course locally at about €22.
mapQuery: Accademia della Ventricina, Contrada Ragna 61, Scerni CH, Italy

name: ADI Apicoltura
desc: The serious organic honey house in Italy’s honey town, with proper bookable visits year-round — so you don’t need the festival, which falls six days after you leave. Three tiers: €15 tour and tasting, €25 with cheese and salumi, €50 adding the actual apiary or an apitherapy session.
mapQuery: ADI Apicoltura, Tornareccio CH, Italy

name: Cesarine home cooks
desc: The home-cook network, and the best match for an unfussy family kitchen. Real listings nearby include pallotte cacio e ova at €115pp (max 6, English spoken, 5.0 from 27 reviews), maccheroni alla chitarra with ravioli and tiramisù at €135, and sourdough at €100. Address given after booking. No host in Lanciano or Vasto despite older listings.
mapQuery: Cesarine home cooks, Montesilvano PE, Italy

name: BeCountry — make your own cheese
desc: The only properly hands-on cheese workshop I could verify in reach — you turn fresh milk into cheese and ricotta yourself, forage herbs when possible, then eat lunch with local wine. €80pp, three hours, 10:00–13:30 — but the calendar currently shows only past sold-out dates, so contact them before counting on September.
mapQuery: BeCountry — make your own cheese, Pietranico PE, Italy

name: Spiaggia La Foce
desc: Your closest sea — 1.3 km straight down the hill. The comune's biggest beach, around 600 m of pebble and shingle with transverse rock spurs. Most equipped and most used, campsite with bar and restaurant 100 m back.
address: Contrada Foce, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Spiaggia La Foce, Contrada Foce, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

name: Vallevò
desc: The postcard one. Fishing harbour, the fishermen's circolo, two trabocchi, a gelateria. Pebble, gravel and coarse sand, mix of free and managed.
address: Vallevo, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Vallevo, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

name: Punta Cavalluccio beach
desc: About 30 m of very fine sand between rocks under a high promontory, with the trabocco and a sea stack. Beautiful, holds about forty people, shaded in the afternoon. Access via the SS16 underpass.
address: Punta Cavalluccio, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy
mapQuery: Punta Cavalluccio, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

name: Fossacesia Marina
desc: Your default proper beach. Long and narrow, white pebbles and pale sand, multiple Blue Flags, both free stretches and stabilimenti, bars, parking, disabled access.
mapQuery: Fossacesia Marina, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: Majellando — dinghy hire, no licence
desc: A 4.5 m gommone for up to five people with no boat licence needed — just a car licence and 18+. Take yourselves along the trabocchi to Acquabella and the Turchino. €120 + fuel for a 3.5-hour half day, €80 sunset; the full-day rate isn’t published, so ask. Runs daily to 30 September, covering your whole stay.
address: Marina del Sole, Fossacesia CH, Italy
mapQuery: Majellando — dinghy hire, no licence, Marina del Sole, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: Freedom Boat
desc: Skippered group cruises along the trabocchi with swim stops, plus dawn and sunset-aperitivo runs. €50pp for 3 hours, €45 at dawn — but there’s a five-person or €250 minimum to sail, which is the real risk in September rather than closure. WhatsApp +39 329 3905663.
address: Marina del Sole, Fossacesia CH, Italy
mapQuery: Freedom Boat, Marina del Sole, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: Lido Punta Le Morge — naturist
desc: The only officially designated naturist beach in Abruzzo, and the only authorised one on the entire Italian Adriatic. Around 200 m of pebbles backed by the Lecceta reserve; the naturist stretch starts about 400 m north of the trabocco. Free, free parking.
address: Lago Dragoni, Torino di Sangro CH, Italy
mapQuery: Lido Punta Le Morge — naturist, Lago Dragoni, Torino di Sangro CH, Italy

name: Ripari di Giobbe
desc: Cliff-foot shelters and eroded hollows above a white-pebble cove — the wildest bit of the coast. Steep wooden staircase down, 15 minutes each way. Reopened June 2026 after years closed, so check.
address: Ripari di Giobbe, Ortona CH, Italy
mapQuery: Ripari di Giobbe, Ortona CH, Italy

name: Acquatica Scuba
desc: The most credible dive operation on this coast. Secca delle Salpe off Fossacesia is the shallow one at 8–20 m, right in front of you; the Elios wreck off Ortona is at 30 m. Also does guided snorkelling. Season May–October, and September water is about 25 °C with 8–15 m visibility — the best of the year.
address: Marina di Pescara, Pescara PE, Italy
mapQuery: Acquatica Scuba, Marina di Pescara, Pescara PE, Italy

name: Punta Aderci nature reserve
desc: The only stretch of undeveloped cliff-and-dune coast left in Abruzzo — about 6 km of trail from Punta Penna. Free, best at sunset. Also a tolerated naturist stretch at Mottagrossa.
address: Riserva Naturale Punta Aderci, Vasto CH, Italy
mapQuery: Punta Aderci nature reserve, Riserva Naturale Punta Aderci, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Majellando — soft rafting on the Sangro
desc: About 7 km and 90 minutes on the water in CE rafts with qualified guides, putting in at the edge of the Serranella wetland. €35 adult, €25 child, departures 10:00 and 17:00, dates published through September. The strongest in-the-water option in the second half of your stay.
mapQuery: Majellando — soft rafting on the Sangro, Sant'Eusanio del Sangro CH, Italy

name: Stella Pescaturismo
desc: A genuine working-boat day: 6:00 to 15:00 aboard the Stella, hauling the nets, marine commentary, a swim stop and a seafood lunch cooked on board. €100pp — but minimum ten people, and the site hasn’t been updated since mid-2024, so phone Bruno (339 2367029) to confirm the boat is running at all this season.
address: Porto di Vasto, Vasto CH, Italy
mapQuery: Stella Pescaturismo, Porto di Vasto, Vasto CH, Italy

name: La Riccia — licence-free RIB, San Domino
desc: 5 m RIB with a 40 hp Honda for up to eight, €300 per boat for eight hours, fuel extra and cash on return. Runs daily to 29 September. No licence needed, and the Capraia marine-reserve permit is included. Two hard rules: you may not take it into the caves, and you must anchor at least 100 m off. Only worth it on an overnight — an eight-hour hire doesn’t fit the 08:40/17:40 day.
address: Porto San Domino, Isole Tremiti FG, Italy
mapQuery: La Riccia — licence-free RIB, San Domino, Porto San Domino, Isole Tremiti FG, Italy

name: Marlin Tremiti — diving
desc: The best-documented Tremiti dive centre: single dive €50 with free nitrox, two dives €90, snorkelling €50, guided boat trips €45. Pairs with the hydrofoil day — the submerged Padre Pio statue is the famous one.
mapQuery: Marlin Tremiti — diving, Isole Tremiti FG, Italy

name: Via Verde dei Trabocchi
desc: 42 km of car-free paved path on the old railway line, sea the whole way, through lit rock tunnels. Join it at the bottom of the Foce or Vallevò lanes. One live caveat: a 2.5 km gap at Lago Dragoni between Fossacesia and Torino di Sangro, closed by coastal erosion, was contracted to reopen 30 August 2026 with a new 80 m steel bridge. Check before planning anything southward. (Good sign: the separate 4 km Casalbordino gap opened 10 August 2026.)
address: Via Verde, Fossacesia Marina, Fossacesia CH, Italy
mapQuery: Via Verde dei Trabocchi, Via Verde, Fossacesia Marina, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: BiciMania / Sorgini
desc: Thirty-year family bike shop with a 120-bike fleet directly on the Via Verde and a proper workshop behind it. Prices aren’t currently published — expect a few euros an hour for city bikes, more for e-bikes. Best combination of proximity, choice and an on-site mechanic. Site says “Riapertura 2026”, so confirm September hours: +39 334 6092310.
mapQuery: BiciMania / Sorgini, Via Lungomare 11, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: Bike + train
desc: Bikes travel free on regional trains showing the bike symbol, so you can ride one-way and train back from Fossacesia–Torino di Sangro or San Vito–Lanciano. You cannot reserve a bike space and Trenitalia warns you can be refused boarding when they fill — travel early, have a fallback train.
address: Stazione Fossacesia-Torino di Sangro, Fossacesia CH, Italy
mapQuery: Bike + train, Stazione Fossacesia-Torino di Sangro, Fossacesia CH, Italy

name: Al Murè
desc: Beach bar and rental kiosk at the foot of your descent — bikes from €3/hr, e-bikes from €8, and SUP boards at €10/hr. Dog-friendly. Listed 7/7 08:00–20:00, but it’s a beach concession, so ring for the week after the 13th.
address: Via Cristoforo Colombo 72, San Vito Chietino CH, Italy
mapQuery: Al Murè, Via Cristoforo Colombo 72, San Vito Chietino CH, Italy

name: Green Road Bike — rental & delivery
desc: The one operator with a verified door-to-door pick-up and drop-off, priced by distance — which matters when the path is 100 m below the house. Open all year by reservation, English spoken, full published tariff: city €20/day, gravel €30, e-bike €40. WhatsApp Davide on +39 388 7210195 and ask for a week rate with the bikes left at the house.
address: Via Cervana, Lido Saraceni, Ortona CH, Italy
mapQuery: Green Road Bike — rental & delivery, Via Cervana, Lido Saraceni, Ortona CH, Italy

name: Officine Forti
desc: Rental plus a real workshop with specialist mechanics — the fallback if something breaks mid-trip. City €20/day, e-bike €40, cargo €50, child trailer €15.
address: Via G. Federico 11, Ortona CH, Italy
mapQuery: Officine Forti, Via G. Federico 11, Ortona CH, Italy

name: BikExplora
desc: Enthusiast shop — full-suspension MTB, gravel, fat bikes — that also delivers, and runs five food-and-wine e-bike day tours (€40–100pp) including a Trabocchi coast day and a ventricina day at Torrebruna. WhatsApp booking on +39 392 8120120.
address: Via Martiri Istriani 1, Vasto CH, Italy
mapQuery: BikExplora, Via Martiri Istriani 1, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Bike Park Majella
desc: MTB school for children and guided excursions for competent riders on forest trails at Piana delle Mele. Bike, helmet and gloves supplied, €10–€15. Booking obligatory; September opening isn’t published, so confirm.
address: Piana delle Mele, Guardiagrele CH, Italy
mapQuery: Bike Park Majella, Piana delle Mele, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: Blockhaus
desc: The defining road climb of the region and a Giro monument — 31 km at 6.4% average, 13.4% max, 2,000 m of ascent to 2,068 m, twenty hairpins, sea views from the top. Three sides; the Lettomanoppello one is the feared one. Rent a road bike from Cycling Abruzzo at Miglianico rather than a coastal hybrid.
mapQuery: Blockhaus, Roccamorice PE, Italy

name: Circolo Ippico Jack O'Neill
desc: Rides through the Punta Aderci reserve and along the beach, with dawn and sunset options. Open Tue–Sun, year-round — book the sunset one. One page now says riders need to be 14+ with certification, and the €30/€40 prices have gone from the site, so phone 340 696 5819 to confirm beginners are still taken.
mapQuery: Circolo Ippico Jack O'Neill, SS16 78, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Parco Avventura Majella
desc: 250-odd treetop obstacles, Tibetan bridges and zip lines in beech and pine shade at Piana delle Mele, graded from toddler to adult. Roughly €22–30 adult. Weekends and holidays by September — phone before driving up.
address: Piana delle Mele, Guardiagrele CH, Italy
mapQuery: Parco Avventura Majella, Piana delle Mele, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: Vertical Park
desc: A 150 m equipped rock route up a limestone wall with sea views, cave sections and cable-and-rung passages — via ferrata without owning any kit. Guide, helmet and harness included, about three hours. Ages 12+, needs a head for heights. Weekends by appointment; September is prime season.
mapQuery: Vertical Park, Pennapiedimonte CH, Italy

name: Canyoning — Abruzzo Adventures
desc: Guided gorge descent with waterfalls and natural slides, 2–3 hours, wetsuit and helmet provided, hot shower after. Ages 12–55; you needn’t be a strong swimmer but you must be happy in water. Same outfit runs a stable and off-road buggies, so you can double up.
mapQuery: Canyoning — Abruzzo Adventures, Palena CH, Italy

name: Maja Quad
desc: Hourly quad hire and guided trails in the Valle Giumentina on tracks no car reaches, plus a night safari for wildlife. Small family operation — call Piero on +39 333 575 8556, don’t email.
mapQuery: Maja Quad, Abbateggio PE, Italy

name: Climbing taster — Majellando
desc: Half-day on real rock with a UIAGM alpine guide, insurance included. Genuinely beginner-friendly but assumes reasonable fitness. €40pp, minimum two, about 3.5 hours, June–September and usually weekends.
mapQuery: Climbing taster — Majellando, Roccamorice PE, Italy

name: Jeep safari — MajellaTrekking
desc: Sunset 4x4 wildlife watching with a specialist park guide and Swarovski optics — 13 km, 8 of them on unmade track. Almost no walking, but you sit still and silent for two hours. €40 adult, €45 for the night version. The red deer rut starts mid-September, which is exactly why this is worth doing on your dates. Book by 18:00 the day before.
mapQuery: Jeep safari — MajellaTrekking, Campo di Giove AQ, Italy

name: Tandem paragliding
desc: Twenty to thirty minutes airborne off Rocca di Calascio or Celano, no experience needed. €120pp cash through Majellando, plus €20 for GoPro footage; under 110 kg, no vertigo. Abruzzo Fly at Tocco da Casauria and Scafa is the nearer alternative but doesn’t publish prices.
mapQuery: Tandem paragliding, Rocca Calascio, Calascio AQ, Italy

name: Lecceta di Torino di Sangro
desc: Four waymarked trails from 700 m to 2.5 km through coastal holm-oak wood running down to the Sangro river mouth, past the war cemetery. Genuinely shaded — the best hot-day walk on the coast, and everything else here is unshaded. Free, no permit.
address: Lecceta di Torino di Sangro, Torino di Sangro CH, Italy
mapQuery: Lecceta di Torino di Sangro, Torino di Sangro CH, Italy

name: Cammino di San Tommaso — final stage
desc: The pilgrim route from St Peter’s in Rome ends at Ortona cathedral, which holds the apostle’s relics. Stage 16, Crecchio to Ortona, is a car-shuttle day through rolling Chieti farmland with a cathedral at the end. Credentials from the association.
mapQuery: Cammino di San Tommaso — final stage, Crecchio CH, Italy

name: Gessopalena Vecchia
desc: A whole medieval quarter built of and on gypsum, blown up by the Wehrmacht in December 1943 and never reoccupied. White rock, roofless shells — a small bleached Pompeii. Free, walkable in an hour. The best uncanny half-day near you.
mapQuery: Gessopalena Vecchia, Gessopalena CH, Italy

name: Gole di San Martino
desc: A slot barely 2 m wide between vertical walls — the door of the Majella — with an excavated monastery at its mouth. Legend says St Martin tore it open by hand. Free. Rockfall is a real hazard, avoid in bad weather.
mapQuery: Gole di San Martino, Fara San Martino CH, Italy

name: Riserva Lago di Serranella
desc: The real birdwatching site near you — WWF wetland at the Sangro and Aventino confluence, a key migration stopover, so mid-September is good timing. Four flat paths, free to walk. Hide access and guided visits by reservation on 0872 99281.
address: Riserva Lago di Serranella, Sant'Eusanio del Sangro CH, Italy
mapQuery: Riserva Lago di Serranella, Sant'Eusanio del Sangro CH, Italy

name: Majexperience — guides
desc: Five registered mountain and nature guides on your side of the Majella, with an online booking calendar. They run many of the national park’s listed excursions — typically €12 adult, €5 for 12–18, guide and insurance included. +39 389 11 38 621.
mapQuery: Majexperience — guides, Fara San Martino CH, Italy

name: Grotta Sant'Angelo
desc: An enormous rock overhang swallowing the ruins of an 11th-c. Benedictine church — two walls, an apse with hanging arches, stone basins where pilgrims collected water. A pre-Christian site of the goddess Bona before it was St Michael's. Free, 1.5 hr loop.
mapQuery: Grotta Sant'Angelo, Palombaro CH, Italy

name: Calanchi di Bucchianico
desc: Clay badlands right on the Chieti hinterland doorstep — raw eroded fins, EU-protected, no infrastructure. Free, roadside viewing and local walking routes.
mapQuery: Calanchi di Bucchianico, Bucchianico CH, Italy

name: Buonanotte (Montebello sul Sangro)
desc: A medieval village abandoned to landslide in the 1960s — belongings still inside the houses and contemporary art installed among the ruins. Shown at the Venice Architecture Biennale. Free, walk in. The hillside is still moving — stay out of interiors.
mapQuery: Buonanotte (Montebello sul Sangro), Montebello sul Sangro CH, Italy

name: Castello di Roccascalegna
desc: Fairytale castle on a bare rock needle, reached by a stepped ridge path. The legend: a baron who reinstated ius primae noctis, was stabbed by a bride, and left a bloody handprint on the stone that reappears however often it's scrubbed. Booking advised.
mapQuery: Castello di Roccascalegna, Roccascalegna CH, Italy

name: Grotta del Cavallone
desc: Europe's highest show cave at 1,475 m, reached by a survivor of a nearly extinct machine — an open two-seat basket lift creeping 20 minutes across the valley — then 280 rock-cut steps. D'Annunzio set La figlia di Iorio here. The 2026 September schedule isn't published — ring 351 929 3832 before driving, it closes a lot.
mapQuery: Grotta del Cavallone, Taranta Peligna CH, Italy

name: Juvanum
desc: A Roman forum, theatre and temple podium marooned on an empty 1,000 m plateau with nothing around them. Excellent late light. Park always free; museum weekends only in September.
mapQuery: Juvanum, Montenerodomo CH, Italy

name: Cascate del Verde
desc: The highest natural waterfall in the Apennines, dropping in three leaps into a dank green amphitheatre. Confirm hours and fee before driving.
mapQuery: Cascate del Verde, Borrello CH, Italy

name: Tombe rupestri di San Liberatore
desc: Three sarcophagus-shaped graves, a niche and a tiny chapel with a rainwater basin, cut into a 20 m rock wall by an 8th–9th-century hermit community. Free and easy — path from the abbey forecourt, ford the shallow river.
mapQuery: Tombe rupestri di San Liberatore, Serramonacesca PE, Italy

name: Grotta dei Piccioni
desc: Neolithic sanctuary of the Earth Mother — excavation found stone circles containing human remains, interpreted as sacrifices. Advance reservation at the Park office required.
mapQuery: Grotta dei Piccioni, Bolognano PE, Italy

name: Eremo di Santo Spirito a Majella
desc: Celestine V's mother house, terraced onto a cliff in the Valle dell'Orfento — the grandest of the Majella hermitages, and you can drive to the door. Church free, monastery €5 self-guided.
mapQuery: Eremo di Santo Spirito a Majella, Roccamorice PE, Italy

name: Eremo di San Bartolomeo in Legio
desc: A long stone gallery pressed under a rock lip on a cliff face, reached by steps carved into the rock. Always open, free, about 30 minutes each way. Punishing in full sun, hazardous in rain.
mapQuery: Eremo di San Bartolomeo in Legio, Roccamorice PE, Italy

name: Sunset to stars on the Majella
desc: A 19:00 start from Fonte Tettone at La Majelletta, 1,300 m — 4 km, two hours, grade T, €20 adult and €10 child. High, dark, and looking down over both mountain and sea. Majambiente at Caramanico run similar astronomy walks in the Orfento.
mapQuery: Sunset to stars on the Majella, Fonte Tettone, Pretoro CH, Italy

name: Valle dell'Orfento — Sentiero delle Scalelle
desc: A mule track then a narrow path down to the Orfento torrent, wooden bridges and steep stone stairs. 90 minutes, 120 m of ascent, grade E, cool and shaded with dippers on the water. Needs a free registration — online or at the Caramanico visitor centre, September hours 9–13 and 15–19. Boots compulsory and enforced.
mapQuery: Valle dell'Orfento — Sentiero delle Scalelle, Caramanico Terme PE, Italy

name: Corvara
desc: Village clinging to a rock spur, largely emptied. Used as a film set — and fake shop plaques from the production are still nailed up among the real abandoned houses, which is its own kind of unsettling.
mapQuery: Corvara PE, Italy

name: Roccacaramanico
desc: Down to four residents in the 1970s and openly called a ghost village; since half-bought as second homes, so it's a beautifully preserved half-dead village rather than a ruin field. Free, drive in.
address: Roccacaramanico, Sant'Eufemia a Maiella PE, Italy
mapQuery: Roccacaramanico, Sant'Eufemia a Maiella PE, Italy

name: Calanchi di Atri
desc: Around 380 hectares of grey clay pinnacles usually described as lunar. Free, no gates, three loops from 800 m to 6 km. A small pagan altar-stone sits on the middle route.
address: Riserva Calanchi di Atri, Atri TE, Italy
mapQuery: Calanchi di Atri, Riserva Calanchi di Atri, Atri TE, Italy

name: Bosco di Sant'Antonio
desc: 550 hectares of monumental candelabra-pruned beech and maple — an old sacred grove. Flat, fully shaded, about an hour, grade T. Perfect for a hot afternoon, and it pairs with Pescocostanzo’s old town and its bobbin-lace museum.
address: Bosco di Sant'Antonio, Pescocostanzo AQ, Italy
mapQuery: Bosco di Sant'Antonio, Pescocostanzo AQ, Italy

name: Saepinum / Altilia
desc: A complete small Roman town — walls, gates, forum, theatre — with 18th-century farmhouses built straight into the theatre cavea using Roman seating as walls, and a sheep-drove road still running through the middle. Free, daily 08:15–19:15. Best value on the list.
mapQuery: Saepinum / Altilia, Altilia, Sepino CB, Italy

name: Ecotur — bear watching
desc: The most reliable scheduled wildlife programme in Abruzzo — bear watching every Tuesday and Saturday through September, plus wolf tracking. Be realistic: the 2026 estimate puts the whole Marsican bear population at 81 animals, almost all in this park, so a guided evening is the only sensible way to try.
mapQuery: Ecotur — bear watching, Pescasseroli AQ, Italy

name: Deer rut — guided evening
desc: Saturday 19 September, 15:00–19:30, Pianoro Campitelli to the Altopiano dei Biscurri. About five hours, grade E, €20pp including guide and insurance, telephoto observation at distance, with chamois, golden eagle and wolf also possible. The rut is the genuine wildlife spectacle of your window.
mapQuery: Deer rut — guided evening, Alfedena AQ, Italy

name: Museo Universitario di Chieti
desc: Five human mummies in a controlled-atmosphere case, palaeopathology arranged by parasites, tumours and trauma, and 1.7-billion-year-old stromatolites — inside a 1934 rationalist Fascist dopolavoro palace whose staircase spirals around two enormous stone fasci. €3; Tue–Fri 9–19:30, weekends 15–20, closed Mondays.
address: Piazza Trento e Trieste 1, Chieti CH, Italy
mapQuery: Museo Universitario di Chieti, Piazza Trento e Trieste 1, Chieti CH, Italy

name: Bagno Borbonico
desc: The Genti d'Abruzzo museum sits inside the Bourbon fortress, and its Risorgimento wing is the old political prison — you walk the cells as part of the normal visit. (A theatrical staging existed in 2018 but no longer runs.) Museum closed Sundays.
address: Via delle Caserme 24, Pescara PE, Italy
mapQuery: Bagno Borbonico, Via delle Caserme 24, Pescara PE, Italy

name: MACTE
desc: Surreal in context — a serious contemporary art museum in a fishing port, built around a prize collection the town has been accumulating since 1955. Free, Wed–Sat.
mapQuery: MACTE, Via Giappone, Termoli CB, Italy

name: Museo del Treno
desc: Volunteer-run railway museum on the ground floor of a working station. Two locomotives, eight historic carriages, and a 1925 freight wagon converted into a screening room. Free.
address: Stazione di Montesilvano, Montesilvano PE, Italy
mapQuery: Museo del Treno, Stazione di Montesilvano, Montesilvano PE, Italy

name: MOM — Museo dell'Orso Marsicano
desc: Five rooms devoted entirely to one animal, folklore included, in a former convent — with a reconstructed forest, a soundscape, and a fenced enclosure of non-releasable brown bears nearby. From September: weekends only, mornings 9–13, €3.
mapQuery: MOM — Museo dell'Orso Marsicano, Palena CH, Italy

name: Museo Geopaleontologico
desc: One obsessive private collection of Miocene fossil fish, crustaceans and bird feathers dug from the Aventino valley over decades, installed in the Castello Ducale. Free. Same village as the bear museum.
mapQuery: Museo Geopaleontologico, Castello Ducale, Palena CH, Italy

name: Santuario del Volto Santo
desc: A 17×24 cm veil so fine it's nearly invisible, bearing a male face with no trace of pigment, visible from both sides — and the subject of a long-running fight with the Turin Shroud camp. You climb behind the altar and look through it.
mapQuery: Santuario del Volto Santo, Via Cappuccini 26, Manoppello PE, Italy

name: Centerba Toro distillery
desc: 70% ABV green herbal liqueur, made since 1817 when Beniamino Toro built it in his pharmacy from a Benedictine recipe. Herbs still hand-gathered on Monte Morrone. Prescribed as a cholera remedy in Naples in 1836. No public tour advertised — phone and ask, but buy it regardless.
address: Via Tiburtina Valeria, Tocco da Casauria PE, Italy
mapQuery: Centerba Toro distillery, Via Tiburtina Valeria, Tocco da Casauria PE, Italy

name: Museo Confetti Pelino
desc: Three centuries of sugared-almond technology inside a working Liberty-style factory — 18th-c. mills and mortars, a wall of European patents, the 1893 electric motor, and Sulmona's first telephone. Free. Slots against the 19–20 Sept antiques market.
address: Via Stazione Introdacqua 55, Sulmona AQ, Italy
mapQuery: Museo Confetti Pelino, Via Stazione Introdacqua 55, Sulmona AQ, Italy

name: Museo dei Misteri
desc: Possibly the best single thing on this list. Thirteen iron ingegni from the 1740s — hidden armatures that suspend living children in mid-air, apparently unsupported, above the Corpus Domini procession. Devotional machines that look exactly like torture rigs. Mon–Sat 16:00–18:00, free.
mapQuery: Museo dei Misteri, Via Trento, Campobasso CB, Italy

name: Pontificia Fonderia Marinelli
desc: Papal bell foundry casting bronze by essentially medieval method since 1040 — routinely called the oldest family business on earth. Clay moulds, the pit, molten bronze, and a retired master playing a concert on the foundry bells. Booking mandatory, tours 12:00 and 16:00.
address: Via Felice D'Onofrio 14, Agnone IS, Italy
mapQuery: Pontificia Fonderia Marinelli, Via Felice D'Onofrio 14, Agnone IS, Italy

name: Museo del Profumo
desc: 1,500 perfumes with their original price tags in mother-of-pearl vitrines. The backstory is the strange part: the village's knife-grinders emigrated after the war and ended up running 500+ perfume shops in Rome alone. Reservation only, 24h notice.
address: Via del Profumo 1, Sant'Elena Sannita IS, Italy
mapQuery: Museo del Profumo, Via del Profumo 1, Sant'Elena Sannita IS, Italy

name: Museo dei Ferri Taglienti
desc: A village that has done nothing but blades for 400 years. Museum of knives and scissors with a live forge where masters hammer blades in front of you. 24 hours' booking notice.
mapQuery: Museo dei Ferri Taglienti, Via Garibaldi, Frosolone IS, Italy

name: Sartoria Flocco
desc: Verina Flocco’s sartoria on the corso — a ladies’ and alterations laboratorio, and the nearest tailor for a repair or a fitting. Hours aren’t published, so ring 0872 700435 first. Mid-September means normal trading, but expect Saturday-afternoon and Monday-morning closures.
mapQuery: Sartoria Flocco, Corso Bandiera 63, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Ceramiche d'Arte Liberati
desc: Family workshop founded 1980, now second generation — a genuine production lab doing crystallized glazes, cuerda seca and sculpture, not a gift shop. Showroom and workshop Mon–Fri 8:30–12:30 / 15:00–19:00, Saturday full day, closed Sunday. They sell online too. +39 0871 300750.
mapQuery: Ceramiche d'Arte Liberati, Villamagna CH, Italy

name: Creta Rossa
desc: A teaching studio going since 2001: wheel, hand-building, majolica decoration, raku, plus one-off sessions and workshops for adults and children. Your best bet for a hands-on couple of hours. Phone 349 5843336 to arrange — prices aren’t published.
address: Piazza del Tomolo 3, Vasto CH, Italy
mapQuery: Creta Rossa, Piazza del Tomolo 3, Vasto CH, Italy

name: Fabio Amoroso
desc: The most interesting of the Rapino ceramic revivalists — exhibits at the Guardiagrele artisan show, teaches courses, has shown experimental work at the ceramics museum. Message him about a private session.
mapQuery: Fabio Amoroso, Rapino CH, Italy

name: La Nicchia dell'Artista
desc: Terenzio Michelli, the other young Rapino ceramicist working the local tradition — including the galletto col fischio, the whistling cockerel. Sells direct from the studio. Message ahead.
mapQuery: La Nicchia dell'Artista, Rapino CH, Italy

name: Ceramiche Artistiche Tasca
desc: Long-established Rapino bottega. Turn up, but ring first — 0871 801186.
address: Via XXIV Maggio 22, Rapino CH, Italy
mapQuery: Ceramiche Artistiche Tasca, Via XXIV Maggio 22, Rapino CH, Italy

name: Arterame & Ferro
desc: Lelio Di Sciascio's wrought-iron and copper workshop — lamps, furniture, fireplace and nautical pieces. Mon–Fri 09:00–18:30. Caveat: the site reads as e-commerce rather than an open forge, so WhatsApp or ring +39 340 2797202 before turning up expecting to watch someone work.
mapQuery: Arterame & Ferro, Via Grele 14, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: Museo dell'Artigianato Artistico Abruzzese
desc: Unlike the big August artisan show, it runs outside the summer — but current hours couldn’t be confirmed, so check before building the day around it. Pair it with the forge, the goldsmiths and the ceramicists at Rapino for one excellent day.
mapQuery: Museo dell'Artigianato Artistico Abruzzese, Guardiagrele CH, Italy

name: GuilmiArtProject
desc: Rural artist-in-residence programme, still active in 2026, with public installations and workshops in the village. Email to ask what's on in September.
mapQuery: GuilmiArtProject, Guilmi CH, Italy

name: Di Quinzio Sartoria
desc: Proper men’s abiti su misura plus alterations. Mon–Fri 9–13 / 15–19, Sat mornings. +39 327 699 9830. Worth knowing: Brioni’s factory at Penne is a working production site with no visits, no outlet (closed 2017) and no museum — don’t drive there.
address: Via Piero Gobetti 18, Pescara PE, Italy
mapQuery: Di Quinzio Sartoria, Via Piero Gobetti 18, Pescara PE, Italy

name: La Casa per le Arti
desc: Four generations of applied arts run by sculptor Walter Zuccarini — gilding, carving, inlay, stone and wood sculpture, restoration. Runs actual courses; ask what falls in your dates.
mapQuery: La Casa per le Arti, Via Spilorzi 7, Chieti CH, Italy

name: Lanificio Merlino
desc: An 1870 wool mill — but visited as heritage rather than a working floor. Guided tours around €10 on scheduled dates via MajExperience. Traditional angel-motif Abruzzese blankets still made in a reduced way.
mapQuery: Lanificio Merlino, Taranta Peligna CH, Italy

name: Belisario Camicie
desc: Made-to-measure handmade shirts with atelier fittings at Marina di Città Sant’Angelo — the standout craft-tailoring experience in reach, and a shirt is a fitting that works on holiday timescales. 085 959134.
address: Viale Matrino 161, Citta Sant'Angelo PE, Italy
mapQuery: Belisario Camicie, Viale Matrino 161, Citta Sant'Angelo PE, Italy

name: Museo del Merletto a Tombolo
desc: Bobbin lace still taught and made in town, with lacemakers sometimes working live in the museum. Book on arrival day.
mapQuery: Museo del Merletto a Tombolo, Piazza Municipio, Pescocostanzo AQ, Italy

name: Ceramiche Simonetti
desc: In Italy's majolica town since the 1500s — the family most often found actually decorating in front of visitors, and their Casa d'Arte branch still uses a pedal wheel and a wood kiln. Their site blocked checking, so confirm by phone before the 1h50 drive.
address: Via Gentile Carmine 32, Castelli TE, Italy
mapQuery: Ceramiche Simonetti, Via Gentile Carmine 32, Castelli TE, Italy

name: Ceramiche De Fabritiis
desc: Hand-painted by master painters. Showroom on Via F.A. Grue with a separate workshop. Mon–Fri 10–12 / 14–18, Sat mornings.
address: Via F.A. Grue 24, Castelli TE, Italy
mapQuery: Ceramiche De Fabritiis, Via F.A. Grue 24, Castelli TE, Italy

name: Museo delle Ceramiche di Castelli
desc: Majolica from the great 16th–18th-c. workshops under the Gran Sasso, plus the school's 500-piece international contemporary collection. Free — but weekends only, so it has to be Sat 12 or Sat 19.
mapQuery: Museo delle Ceramiche di Castelli, Salita Paradiso, Castelli TE, Italy

name: Orafi Rotolo 1884
desc: Laboratorio in vetrina — the bench is the shop window, so you watch the goldsmith work. Makes the presentosa by cuttlebone casting. Walk in.
mapQuery: Orafi Rotolo 1884, Scanno AQ, Italy

name: Birreria La Porta
desc: Scruffy brewpub down a blind alley in the old walls, rock and punk on the stereo, own and local craft on tap. Closest thing to Pescara's punk energy near you — and it probably pours Monsters Factory, the gore-themed beer outfit on the same street.
mapQuery: Birreria La Porta, Via Bastioni 62, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Corner
desc: More polished than scruffy, but has a point of view: Thursday sommelier tastings, Friday cocktail masterclass, free Saturday DJ sets and live from 20:00. Closed Wednesdays.
address: Corso Trento e Trieste 121, Lanciano CH, Italy
mapQuery: Corner, Corso Trento e Trieste 121, Lanciano CH, Italy

name: Casa del Popolo 'La Conviviale'
desc: A genuine ARCI circolo — assemblies, talks, gigs. The most locals-only, least touristy room on this list. Bring an ARCI card.
mapQuery: Casa del Popolo 'La Conviviale', Vasto CH, Italy

name: Scumm
desc: Pirate-and-Monkey-Island-themed ARCI live club built into the 16th-c. Bourbon fortress walls, with a 100-cap gig room in the vaults. Punk, hardcore, experimental. Confirmed gig Tuesday 15 September: Grito Exclamac!ón (and Stormo on Fri 25, after you leave).
address: Via delle Caserme 38, Pescara PE, Italy
mapQuery: Scumm, Via delle Caserme 38, Pescara PE, Italy

name: Radicale
desc: The strongest natural wine address in the region — opened 2025 by Davide Gentile of the Lammidia winery with a chef ex-Mugaritz. Spontaneous-ferment bottles, kombucha, fifteen sharing plates, a social table among the racks.
address: Via dei Bastioni 10, Pescara PE, Italy
mapQuery: Radicale, Via dei Bastioni 10, Pescara PE, Italy

name: Spazio Matta

mapQuery: Grotte di Stiffe, San Demetrio ne' Vestini AQ, Italy

name: Isole Tremiti (via Termoli)

The 31 Aug–20 Sept timetable is 08:40 out daily and 17:40 back Mon–Sat — eight hours on the islands — with an extra 11:10 out on Saturdays and 15:00 on Fridays. Your last day, the 20th, is the last day of this timetable; from the 21st it collapses to one boat each way. Avoid Sunday: the return is 16:00 or 18:30, so you get either six hours or ten. On arrival do the 3-hour archipelago boat tour with five swim stops (~€45, leaves 10:00 and 11:00 from the San Domino quay), then San Nicola's fortress abbey. No cars on the islands — park at the Autoparcheggio del Porto in Termoli, guarded, under 100 m from boarding, about €6 a day.

mapQuery: Isole Tremiti (via Termoli), Porto di Termoli, Termoli CB, Italy

There’s a 75-minute version at €27 but it skips the caves. Buy at the quay on arrival.
address: Porto San Domino, Isole Tremiti FG, Italy
mapQuery: Luna Navigazione — giro delle isole, Porto San Domino, Isole Tremiti FG, Italy

mapQuery: NLG Santa Lucia — the rough-sea boat, Porto di Termoli, Termoli CB, Italy

mapQuery: Private boat to the Tremiti — Abruzzo Skipper, Marina di San Pietro, Termoli CB, Italy

mapQuery: Santo Stefano di Sessanio AQ, Italy

mapQuery: Gelateria Le Verì, Vallevò, Rocca San Giovanni CH, Italy

desc: The historic Camplone house and its capriccetti, plus a bench of Abruzzese flavours you won't find on the coast: crema Aurum, liquirizia di Atri, zafferano dell'Aquila, confetto di Sulmona, mosto cotto, scrucchiata d'uva, the torroncino under dark chocolate. Only if you're already in Pescara for the evening — pair it with Rabottini or a train-in night.

name: SottoSale Osteria di Mare
desc: The de Sanctis family's seafood osteria by the marina, “da Patrizia e il Cavaliere” — Trabocchi-coast cooking done on solid ground, which makes it the obvious fallback the nights the wind shuts the trabocchi down. Fritture, cozze, local fish, honest prices, sea view, ~400 reviews. Via Cristoforo Colombo 78.

name: Osteria 101
desc: If Frapa is the stand-in for your Amici della Forchetta, this is the other one — arguably closer. Corso Roma in the old centre, family-run, walls hung with the last century's kitchen tools, barely a menu: you eat what they bring. Rintrocilo (Lanciano's fat square bucatino) with ragù, pallotte cacio e ova, the famous hand-rolled mega olive all'ascolana, rabbit with scamorza. Humble prices. Open every lunch plus Tue–Sat dinner — crucially it does Sunday lunch, 12:30–15:00, but no Sunday dinner, and Monday is lunch only (your only Monday is the 14th). Corso Roma 115/117, 327 0469186.

name: Bracevia — A Tutta Pecora
desc: Grew out of a travelling arrosticini grill mounted on a vintage yellow Fiat 500; the osteria sits on Piazza Sirena by the sea. All sheep — hand-made mutton arrosticini, pecora alla callara, sheep burger, boards of Farindola and Scanno cheese. Cheap and lively, €10–25. Gambero Rosso rate the arrosticini among Italy's best. Closed Tuesdays; dinner only from 18:30. Piazza Sirena 9, +39 371 536 0722.

name: La Grotta dei Raselli
desc: Literally carved into the rock up at Comino — Franco Spadaccini's kitchen since 1999, wife Anna Maria in the room. Abruzzese cooking with a light touch: own bread and pasta from recovered heritage grains, agnello IGP, game, ravioli with sheep ricotta, veg from the family plot, and a cellar that runs to dozens of pages. Dressier than a rough osteria but Slow Food class it as one. Book — the last stretch of road and parking are awkward. 0871 808292.
